office: Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER)
subject: Warning Letter — CGMP violations, licensed biological products
content:
[SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — fictional letter written for the WarnSync reference implementation. Not a real FDA record.]

Dear Dr. Feng:

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration inspected your licensed biologics manufacturing facility from December 1 to December 12, 2025. This letter describes significant violations of current good manufacturing practice, 21 CFR parts 210, 211, and 600 through 680.

1. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm attributed three consecutive bioburden excursions in the upstream suite to sampling error and resumed processing without identifying a root cause. Two of the affected lots were released for distribution.

2. Your firm failed to report to the agency a deviation from applicable current good manufacturing practice regulations that may affect the safety, purity, or potency of a distributed product (21 CFR 600.14). The temperature excursion affecting lot SB-25-114 during shipment on November 9, 2025 was documented in your quality system on November 12, 2025 and had not been reported at the time of the inspection.

3. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile (21 CFR 211.113(b)). Your firm's aseptic connection procedure permits operators to reconnect single-use tubing assemblies after a failed integrity test without an intervening line clearance.

This letter is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of violations. You are responsible for investigating and determining the causes of any violations and for preventing their recurrence.

4. Your firm failed to establish and maintain a system for implementing corrective actions arising from environmental monitoring of aseptic processing areas (21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iv)). Recovery of a mold species at the fill line during the September 2025 campaign was recorded as an isolated finding; the same species was recovered on four subsequent occasions before any corrective action was initiated.

5. Your firm failed to maintain records concurrently with the performance of each significant step in the manufacture of the product (21 CFR 600.12(b)). Batch records for the drug substance suite were completed at the end of each shift from operator notebooks, and the notebooks were discarded after transcription.

Reporting obligations. Under 21 CFR 600.14, a licensed manufacturer must report to the agency each deviation from applicable regulations or from applicable standards in the biologics license application that may affect the safety, purity, or potency of a distributed product, as soon as possible and in no case later than 45 calendar days from the date of discovery. Your firm's procedure requires reporting only after completion of the associated investigation, which places your firm outside the required timeframe whenever an investigation exceeds that period.

Conclusion and response. This letter is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of violations. Within fifteen working days of receipt of this letter, notify this office in writing of the specific steps you have taken to correct these violations. Include an explanation of each step being taken to prevent the recurrence of similar violations, and documentation showing that the corrections have been completed.
